messages:
arjun: Quick question — we've been seeing KMS unwrap spikes tied to a few hot DEKs. Thinking about combining traffic shaping + per-key caching + rotation splay. Any gotchas we should watch for? @molly @sam :thinking:

molly: Yep, saw this with a large customer last quarter. Short summary: local DEK cache per node + probabilistic refresh, plus token-bucket smoothing for KMS calls. Stratify by customer tier so free-tier burst doesn't kill our KMS QPS. :+1:

sam: Adding: detect hotkeys (DEKs used > threshold reqs/min) and switch to aggressive local caching/backoff for those keys. For rotation, splay KEK rotations across nodes and time windows to avoid a thundering herd. Also consider a tiny jitter on unwrap retry.

arjun: Sounds good. Two product/security questions: 1) How do we preserve an auditable link back to KMS when we serve from cache? 2) For RBAC, do we need to re-check perms on every cached unwrap?

molly: For 1) emit an audit event at unwrap time (KMS call) and store the unwrap_event_id in the cache entry. On cache hits emit a lightweight access log that references unwrap_event_id and caller identity. That keeps the KMS audit trail intact without calling KMS on every request.

molly: For 2) we shouldn't call KMS for auth. Instead: perform RBAC check against our IAM layer on every request, independent of cache. Cache only the cryptographic unwrap result, not the auth decision.

sam: Example cache entry (pseudo):

```
cache_key: dek:<customer_id>:<key_id>
value: {
  dek_blob: <ciphertext>,
  unwrap_event_id: "kms-evt-2026-04-03-xxxx",
  created_at: 1650000000,
  ttl_seconds: 300,
  hot_counter: 423
}
```

sam: Hotkey handling: increment hot_counter on each access and when > HOT_THRESHOLD flip to extended-ttl + suppress KMS unwraps with token-bucket. On cache eviction, write a short tombstone referencing last unwrap_event_id so audit correlator can stitch timeline.

security-bot: ALERT: KMS unwrap error rate for region us-west-2 exceeded 0.3% in the last 5m. Incident channel: #incidents. Ticket: INC-9876.

eve: If we hit KMS errors in prod, runbook idea: 1) increase local cache TTL by a factor of 2 for hot keys, 2) enable graceful degraded path where we serve from previous DEK (if within safety window) while forcing background re-unwraps, 3) open a scoped KEK rotation window if we suspect key compromise. Also notify affected customers.

molly: For rotation splay, proposal: assign rotation windows by node hash modulo 3600s, then apply random jitter up to 60s. Example: schedule = base_time + (node_hash % 3600) + rand(0,60). That spreads unwrap/rewrap work across the hour.

sam: We should also add chaos tests that simulate a single hot customer so the KMS proxy and token-bucket behave correctly. Test plan: ramp client QPS, assert KMS QPS stays under N per region, verify no front-end latency regressions > 95th pct baseline.

arjun: Action items: @molly draft cache schema + audit-field mapping, @sam add hotkey detection prototype and chaos test, @eve write incident mitigations into runbook. I'll file RFC after those. Thanks all. :rocket:
